optimizedDescription.value: Canonical spec IDs use workspace:capabilityPath, normalize bare paths to default, reject unknown workspaces and Windows device segments.

optimizedContext.value:
# Spec ID Format

## Rules
- Canonical ID everywhere: `workspace:capabilityPath`; colon separates workspace, every slash belongs to capability path. Same form in manifests, domain, CLI, `dependsOn`, output.
- No colon means default workspace; `auth/login` normalizes to `default:auth/login`.
- Parse first colon only: prefix workspace, suffix capability path; reject unknown configured workspace. Never infer workspace from slash.
- Reject any capability segment equal case-insensitively to `con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com1`…`com9`, or `lpt1`…`lpt9` on every OS. Whole-segment only: `con-foo` legal. Drive letters have no filesystem meaning.
- Normalize bare IDs at system boundary; domain may assume qualification.
- `change.specDependsOn` keys/references must persist fully qualified.

## Constraints
- Workspace contains neither `/` nor `:`.
- Capability path contains no `:`.
- Separator always `:`; default workspace implicit only for bare input.
